The implementation involves finding the last occurrence of the package separator character, identifying any inner class separator characters, and extracting the relevant part of the class name to get the short class name.

Given this implementation, the issue with adding a semicolon to the end of class names for arrays likely occurs during the processing of array encoding, especially when handling array types. We need to investigate how arrays are processed in the `getShortClassName` method to identify the root cause of the problem.

To pinpoint the exact location of the issue, we may need to trace how arrays are handled within the method and ensure that the processing of array type names follows the expected conventions.
Based on the analysis of the `getShortClassName` method in `ClassUtils`, the likely root cause of the issue where a semicolon is added to the end of class names for arrays lies in the array encoding handling within the method. To address the problem, modifications may be necessary in how arrays are processed to ensure that the short class name for arrays is correctly determined without appending unexpected characters such as semicolons.

To resolve the bug, the following method should be fixed:
```
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)
```
